scope: All fifteen models compared in UniRank v2; external method knowledge, not additional baseline executions.

methods.source_problem: Heterogeneous ranking fields may require different interaction transformations after history aggregation.
methods.reported_mechanism: Target-attention history pooling followed by heterogeneous field/task tokenization and hierarchical HiFormer interaction blocks.
methods.change_from_din: Retains target-aware history pooling and replaces simple downstream concatenation/MLPs with token interactions.
conditions: Field groups carry complementary information after history pooling
risks: Early history pooling still loses event detail
Field-specific parameters increase capacity
checks: Compare token interactions with an equally wide post-pooling MLP
Separate field-specific transformations from depth and parameter count

methods.source_problem: Fine-grained attention and heterogeneous operators can constrain scaling of feature interactions.
methods.reported_mechanism: Target-attention pooling, chunk tokenization, parameter-free token mixing and per-token feed-forward networks.
methods.change_from_din: Changes post-pooling feature interaction while retaining an early target-aware history bottleneck.
conditions: Useful history evidence survives pooling
Dense regular operators fit the available hardware
risks: Chunk groups may not preserve semantic boundaries
More width may explain improvements attributed to mixing
checks: Compare parameter-free mixing against no mixing at matched token dimensions
Compare Chunk, Field and global-access tokenization at matched downstream capacity

methods.source_problem: Categorical, sequential and task representations need controlled information exchange without uniformly dense connectivity.
methods.reported_mechanism: Categorical, sequence and task tokens aggregate into hubs and receive layer-wise gated broadcasts; the benchmark initializes task sequence hubs using task-specific action masks.
methods.change_from_din: Replaces one shared pooled history with repeated task-aware aggregation and broadcasting.
conditions: Feedback types have meaningful complementarity
Task-specific histories have enough support
risks: Rare task hubs can be poorly estimated
Additional task parameters can confound information-flow effects
checks: Compare shared hubs, task hubs and shuffled task routing with matched capacity
Replace gates by fixed or task-independent broadcasts
implementation_notes: The benchmark aggregation code documents mask-free SDPA with zeroed sequence K/V; inspect padding behavior before reuse.

methods.source_problem: Long event sequences can make full interaction costly while local details remain useful.
methods.reported_mechanism: Inner Transformers encode local sequence groups; compressed earlier history interacts with recent queries through subsequent layers.
methods.change_from_din: Uses structured compression and repeated interaction rather than a single attention-pooled vector.
conditions: Grouping retains information needed by the target
Sequence length is sufficient to amortize grouping overhead
risks: A maximum history of100 may leave little long-history advantage
Grouping changes both representation and computation
checks: Compare grouped attention with simple grouped pooling using identical inputs
Report quality and latency by history length; keep all methods within the same100-event limit

methods.source_problem: Separating sequence pooling from feature interaction restricts iterative exchange and scaling.
methods.reported_mechanism: Sequence and non-sequential tokens enter every mixed-attention block, with shared sequence FFNs, token-specific non-sequential FFNs and progressive sequence-token reduction.
methods.change_from_din: Retains event tokens across interaction depth and changes which tokens remain active in later layers.
conditions: Repeated target/context interaction adds information beyond one-shot pooling
risks: Token reduction can discard useful older evidence
Depth and active sequence length change computation together
checks: Compare one-shot readout with repeated interaction at matched active-token cost
Separate progressive reduction from token-specific FFNs
implementation_notes: The benchmark MixedMHA documents mask-free SDPA and full attention used to approximate pyramid reduction. Do not equate this reimplementation with the original paper without checking.

methods.source_problem: Identifier memorization and attribute generalization may compete when all fields use the same representation budget.
methods.reported_mechanism: Separately expanded user/item ID embeddings, target-aware attribute/history pooling and dedicated ID/context/attribute tokens feed token-wise interaction blocks.
methods.change_from_din: Allocates distinct sparse capacity and interaction paths to IDs and attributes.
conditions: Returning users/items have adequate training support
Sparse embedding storage is affordable
risks: Embedding expansion alone may explain gains
Low-frequency or unseen IDs may not benefit
checks: Match total embedding parameters against a uniform-dimension control
Separate ID-token construction from ID embedding expansion; inspect training-frequency slices

methods.source_problem: Sequence refinement and non-sequential interaction may need different operations while exchanging useful summaries.
methods.reported_mechanism: Per-layer sequence encoding, global-query decoding and integration of non-sequential tokens.
methods.change_from_din: Learns global summaries repeatedly while retaining a separate evolving sequence representation.
conditions: A small global-query set captures useful complementary evidence
risks: Query count and repeated attention increase cost
Global queries can collapse to redundant summaries
checks: Compare learned global queries with target-only or fixed pooling queries
Separate sequence encoding, query decoding and feature integration

methods.source_problem: Dense feature interactions and sequence representations may require coordinated refinement rather than independent scaling.
methods.reported_mechanism: Mix non-sequential query tokens, update sequence tokens, cross-attend queries to the sequence, then fuse the representations at each layer.
methods.change_from_din: Makes history retrieval conditional on evolving field queries rather than a single initial target representation.
conditions: Field-conditioned queries retrieve complementary history evidence
risks: Extra layers or query width may dominate observed gains
Repeated retrieval may duplicate the same evidence
checks: Compare evolving queries with shared/frozen queries at matched capacity
Separate non-sequential mixing from repeated sequence retrieval

methods.source_problem: Global field access and grouped interactions require efficient information mixing without losing group structure.
methods.reported_mechanism: Target-aware history summaries are tokenized into global and group tokens, followed by reversible token mixing and per-token FFNs.
methods.change_from_din: Changes field grouping and token transport after the history summary.
conditions: Useful diversity exists across field groups
risks: Early pooling still limits recoverable history detail
Group/token counts change model size
checks: Compare global-only, group-only and combined tokens at matched parameter count
Compare reversible mixing with a capacity-matched ordinary mixer

methods.source_problem: Feature semantics and target-dependent sequence evidence can be obscured by homogeneous interaction functions.
methods.reported_mechanism: Cross-attention to sequence representations combined with feature-specific feed-forward layers in a unified interaction stack.
methods.change_from_din: Uses token-level iterative retrieval and heterogeneous field transformations instead of one pooled readout.
conditions: Field identities carry stable, distinct predictive roles
risks: Field-specific capacity can overfit small or sparse fields
Cross-attention and heterogeneous FFNs alter cost together
checks: Compare shared versus feature-specific FFNs with matched parameters
Separate repeated cross-attention from heterogeneous transformations

methods.source_problem: A single target query and uniform treatment of recent/earlier events can limit interest extraction and field interaction.
methods.reported_mechanism: Fixed and feature-conditioned queries summarize recent and earlier histories, followed by low-rank heterogeneous token mixing.
methods.change_from_din: Changes query construction, history partitioning and downstream interaction; each requires its own attribution control.
conditions: Recent and earlier history have distinguishable utility
Multiple query summaries are complementary
risks: Partitioning and extra query capacity may account for gains
Low-rank mixing can introduce a new representation bottleneck
checks: Compare fixed-only, conditioned-only and mixed queries
Match history partitions and output dimensions when isolating low-rank mixing

methods.source_problem: History compression and heterogeneous feature pipelines can obstruct uniform dense computation.
methods.reported_mechanism: Flatten padded history with user/context fields, chunk-tokenize the combined representation, and apply UniMixing-Lite blocks with paired streams.
methods.change_from_din: Exposes the flattened event representation directly to the tokenizer instead of first applying target-attention pooling.
conditions: Fixed history width and position semantics are meaningful
Tokenizer projection cost fits the budget
risks: Flattened-history projections can have large parameter cost
Padding and truncation conventions can become learned signals
checks: Compare flattening with pooled/grouped history at matched projection parameters
Test padding perturbation and sequence-order sensitivity
implementation_notes: UniRank labels its paired-stream updates an engineering-stable variant; this is a benchmark reimplementation, not verified original-author code.

methods.source_problem: Separate field and sequence pipelines can restrict direct exchange between heterogeneous features and history events.
methods.reported_mechanism: Fields, history events and target become a shared token sequence; full and sliding-window Flex Attention layers provide interaction.
methods.change_from_din: Keeps field and event tokens in the interaction stack rather than reducing history to one vector.
conditions: Direct token exchange provides value beyond compact summaries
Attention kernels are effective at the actual sequence length
risks: Sparse-kernel overhead can dominate at length100
Field/event tokenization changes capacity and operator costs
checks: Compare full, windowed and pooled attention at matched input coverage
Measure actual latency and verify masked-key perturbation invariance
implementation_notes: The benchmark GatedMultiHeadAttentionLayer explicitly documents that invalid keys are not masked inside attention; only final output positions are zeroed. Validate or repair this if adopting the implementation.

methods.source_problem: Full event-token interaction is costly when sequence length and model depth scale together.
methods.reported_mechanism: HSTU-style sequential transduction with hybrid sparse/full attention, item/action representation and layer-dependent active-sequence handling.
methods.change_from_din: Preserves and updates sequence tokens through gated transduction rather than one target-attention summary.
conditions: Sequence dependencies require more than one-shot pooling
Hybrid attention provides savings on the target hardware
risks: Short histories may not amortize sparse-attention setup
Attention pattern, truncation and gating can confound each other
checks: Separate transduction gates from attention sparsity and truncation
Compare equal active-token computation and inspect history-length slices

methods.source_problem: Uniform dense feature connectivity can spend computation on redundant or interfering signals.
methods.reported_mechanism: Target-attention history pooling followed by multi-view competitive sparse filtering and within-view dense fusion; the benchmark uses iterative competitive sparse filtering.
methods.change_from_din: Adds explicit activation selection and multi-view interaction after pooled history.
conditions: Redundant/interfering feature activations can be suppressed without losing rare useful evidence
risks: Activation sparsity does not necessarily yield wall-clock acceleration
Sparse filtering may remove rare-task evidence
checks: Replace competitive filtering with a dense or ordinary-ReLU control at matched capacity
Report measured sparsity separately from training/inference speed and inspect rare tasks
